grades.quote: an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=_ `x0` _will therefore either terminate all previously-launched speculative executions of the addresstranslation algorithm (for the specified ASID, if applicable), or simply wait for them to complete (in which case any address-translation cache entries created will be invalidated by the SFENCE.VMA as appropriate).
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary information about ASID-scoped speculative translation synchronization, without explaining satp ASIDs or SFENCE.VMA operand selection.

grades.quote: Note that writing `satp` does not imply any ordering constraints between page-table updates and subsequent address translations, nor does it imply any invalidation of address-translation caches. If the new address space’s page tables have been modified, or if an ASID is reused, it may be necessary to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction (see Section 12.2.1) after, or in some cases before, writing `satp` .
grades.reason: Explains satp writes, ASID reuse, and possible fencing requirements, but not how ASIDs identify address spaces or select translations.

grades.quote: If _rs1_ = `x0` and _rs2_ ≠ `x0` , the fence orders all reads and writes made to any level of the page tables, but only for the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ . Accesses to _global_ mappings (see Section 12.3.1) are not ordered. The fence also invalidates all address-translation cache entries matching the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ , except for entries containing global mappings.
grades.reason: Explains address-space selection through rs2 and the global-mapping exclusion, but does not explain satp's ASID field.

grades.quote: If _rs1_ ≠ `x0` and _rs2_ ≠ `x0` , the fence orders only reads and writes made to leaf page table entries corresponding to the virtual address in _rs1_ , for the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ . Accesses to global mappings are not ordered. The fence also invalidates all address-translation cache entries that contain leaf page table entries corresponding to the virtual address in _rs1_ and that match the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ , except for entries containing global mappings.
grades.reason: Explains address-and-ASID-scoped SFENCE.VMA synchronization and global exclusions, but not satp's ASID field.
